brief: I read 52 books in 12 months as a founder. These 6 changed how I operate.

slots.subtitle: A year of reading revealed the mental models that separate busy founders from effective ones.
slots.preview1: How to think in bets when capital is tight
slots.preview2: The leverage playbook that killed my hourly rate
slots.preview3: Why systems always beat goals on chaotic Mondays

slots.title: Decisions are
slots.subtitle: Annie Duke taught me to separate outcome quality from decision quality in seconds.
slots.insight1Body: A bad outcome from a good decision is still a win long-term.
slots.insight2Body: Saying 'I'm not sure' forces sharper thinking and faster calibration.
slots.insight3Body: Log predictions to see patterns in how you actually reason.
slots.pullQuote: You can be right and still lose; the goal is calibration, not certainty.

slots.title: Pursue leverage
slots.subtitle: Naval’s almanack reframed how I value my time, equity, and creative output.
slots.insight1Body: Turn your unique skills into scalable assets that compound overnight.
slots.insight2Body: If you can't automate it, delegate it; if not, delete it.
slots.insight3Body: Equity and code beat hourly billing for every founder building wealth.
slots.pullQuote: Earn with your mind, not your time, and let compounding do the heavy lifting.

slots.title: Manage for
slots.subtitle: Andy Grove’s factory logic applies directly to remote teams and product velocity.
slots.insight1Body: Track deliverables shipped, not hours logged, to gauge true velocity.
slots.insight2Body: These are your highest-leverage meetings for catching problems early.
slots.insight3Body: Find the constraint, elevate it, and watch throughput multiply instantly.
slots.pullQuote: The output of a manager is the output of their organization, full stop.

slots.title: Design your
slots.subtitle: James Clear showed me that systems beat goals when the pressure spikes.
slots.insight1Body: Attach a new behaviour to an existing anchor and watch it stick.
slots.insight2Body: Reduce friction for good habits and increase it for bad ones immediately.
slots.insight3Body: One skip is an accident; two is the start of a new pattern.
slots.pullQuote: You do not rise to the level of your goals; you fall to your systems.

slots.title: Embrace the
slots.subtitle: Ben Horowitz taught me that founder pain is the tuition for real leadership.
slots.insight1Body: Layoffs and pivots demand honesty, speed, and radical transparency to survive.
slots.insight2Body: Great operators are made, not hired; invest in coaching them monthly.
slots.insight3Body: Build trust in calm seas so your crew trusts you in storms.
slots.pullQuote: There are no silver bullets, only lead bullets and the courage to fire them.

slots.title: Accept your
slots.subtitle: Oliver Burkeman helped me stop optimizing and start choosing what to neglect.
slots.insight1Body: Freedom comes from realizing your inbox will never be empty anyway.
slots.insight2Body: A fixed schedule forces you to do only what truly matters.
slots.insight3Body: Chasing total optimization is just another distraction from actually living now.
slots.pullQuote: The real measure of your time is what you willingly decide not to do.

slots.ctaBody: The right book at the right moment rewires how you build. Which one will you read first?
